system.summary: Clear Swedish with single words and short phrases in numbers. Each number stands for one letter and each letter has two to four numbers (e 8, 45, 82; a 34, 71, 99; t 37, 74, 102). Seen values run 2-108. u/v/w and i/j/y are each one letter in places; 38 serves å and o, 77 y and ö. In the letters of 27 and 22 May groups are separated by commas and a word ends with a point; in images 104 and 114 the clerk puts a point after every group and leaves a wider space between words.
system.notes: Key: 57 numbers frozen from the glossed runs of images 22-23, 6 values added after the held-out test (72 g, 86 d, 105 ö and 50 k confirmed by the image-75 gloss; 67 p and 7 z from one bare-run word each). Open: 15, 93 (or 97), 97, 108, 2. The catalogue's numbers in the 800s were not met in the passages worked. Exceptions: 79 = t once (image 22, at the fold, could be 74) against m twice in 75; 9 = m once in 75; 31 = s once in the pairs.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on images 104 and 114. Other letters of the same volume carry a contemporary decipherment over the numbers (images 22-23 and 75 were used here). No edition or modern decipherment of these despatches found: two web searches (6 Nov 2026) found only general work on the embassy (Rålamb's diary, ed. C. Callmer, Historiska handlingar 37:3, 1963, not opened; Forss 2021; The Sultan's Procession); the vetting of 5 Nov 2026 found nothing in DECODE, Tomokiyo or Lasry. Not compared with DECODE R4201 (Chifferklaver låda II 82, 1657).

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2258) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built and froze the key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (fetch, crops, contact sheets, decryption, held-out test, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: All 132 images of series 40008933 fetched at low size for contact sheets, and images 22, 23, 75, 104 and 114 at full size, from the Riksarkivet IIIF service, one at a time, 1.6 s apart.

Sign conventions written before any key. Key pairs of images 22-23 (15 glossed runs, about 330 groups) copied with the gloss covered and the gloss read onto separate lines; bare runs of 114 and 104 in two passes each.

Key built from the interlinear pairs of images 22-23 only and frozen (key_frozen.tsv, 57 numbers) before image 75 was cropped or transcribed. The freeze is recorded by file times; the hash was taken afterwards (FROZEN.sha256).

Held-out image 75, graded against its own contemporary gloss with the frozen key: 55 of 64 groups (86%), 4 of 10 words exact, with the clerk's probable slip in 'underhåldet' read as 84; 54 of 65 groups (83%), 3 of 10 words, on the signs as written. Wrong: 79 = m twice, 9 = m once, 77 = ö once. Small test; image 75 had been seen before the freeze at contact-sheet size only.

Bare runs of 114 and 104 decrypted mechanically with key.tsv and read as Swedish with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds the decryptions and fails on any unmarked departure. 114: 31 of 40 words verbatim; 104: 4 of 4.
Two web searches on Rålamb, Vellingk, 1657 and cipher or edition: general work on the embassy only; no edition or decipherment of these despatches.

Independent check by an AI language-model agent that took no part in the solve (VERIFY.md): blind transcription of 297 groups (114 sample, 104, 75), 2 of 297 groups (0.7%) left after settling on crops; key pairs confirmed on the scan; held-out test and mark check reproduced; tamper tests fail as they should. Verdict: confirm, with six minor fixes.

Fixes: 75 L03 written as the signs stand (8 . 4) with the gloss-guided variant on its own line and both scores given; 114 L15 93 marked 93?; key exceptions (31 = s once, the cut 7?, the image-22 79 at the fold) listed; frame table of reading_114.md made to copy the marked reading; scripts set UTF-8 output; freeze recorded. No count changed.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the letter of 27 May 1657 (images 22-23) in the same volume, frozen, tested on the glossed copy of 22 May (image 75), and applied to the bare runs of images 104 and 114, which carry no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Two bare images (104, 114; 35 of their 44 cipher words verbatim from the signs) out of about 30 images with number runs seen on the inspected contact sheets of the 132-image volume (sheets of images 49-72, 85-103 and 121-132 not inspected); the glossed letters are not counted. The two bare images are short runs inside clear letters, marked not prose in the texts. A rough estimate from images, not counted groups.

texts.label: Image 114, letter of June 1657: 30 bare runs
texts.summary: The Porte's assurance and how firmly what they have once written stays written; a mutiny in the camp in which the troops seized the Vizier, brought him to the Sultan and wanted him put to death, until the Sultan got him off by great intercession; the new Mufti, said to plan with the Tatar Khan and the Pasha of Silistra to join forces in support of the Russian.
texts.note: Not prose: a list of 30 short cipher runs (one to three words each, 40 words) set into a despatch written in clear Swedish. Each run is given with our decode with key.tsv and an English gloss. The cipher forms no sentences of its own. The clear text around the runs is an approximate working transcription, given only to place the runs. Words: 31 verbatim from the signs (77.5%), 1 with a marked change (förb{ö/y}n, 77 read as ö), 8 with a hole. The holes are L02, L03, L06, L09 and L14 in the binding (L02 also has the open code 2), and the open codes 97, 15 and 93? in L04, L10 and L15. 22 of the 30 runs read as whole words that fit the clear text around them: a mutiny in the camp in which the troops seized the Vizier, brought him to the Sultan and wanted him put to death, until the Sultan got him off by great intercession; the new Mufti with the Tatar Khan and the Pasha of Silistra joining forces to help the Russian; and 'what has once been written with them stays written'. Two of these runs (uiziren, passa silistrie) rest on the context values 7 z and 67 p. Without those two values, 29 of the 40 words would be verbatim.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Checked as a list of runs against the clear text around them; three runs (L11-L12, L15-L17, L28) checked group for group against the image; the last group of L15 is written over another figure (93 or 97).

texts.label: Image 104, letter after 14 June 1657: one short run
texts.summary: The Vizier uses the interpreter of the Imperial (Habsburg) Resident: 'romerske keiserlige residentens tålk'.
texts.note: Not prose: one cipher run of 33 groups, a four-word phrase set into a despatch written in clear Swedish, with our decode and an English gloss: 'romerske keiserlige residentens tålk', the interpreter of the Roman Imperial (Habsburg) Resident, whom the Vizier uses. All 4 words are verbatim from the signs, with no holes. Every value is in the frozen key except 50 = k, which rests on the contemporary gloss of image 75 and holds at all three places it occurs. There is no ciphered sentence to score, so the entry is labelled not prose rather than read; the phrase itself is deciphered.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Checked as one phrase against the clear text around it; the 33 groups agree with the independent blind transcription (VERIFY.md), and the decode with key_frozen.tsv gives every letter except the one 50 = k.
